skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 gave the full warning at the very start: the Committee and company are the clients, counsel does not represent the witness personally, is not his attorney and cannot advise him, and the company controls waiver and may disclose without his consent.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 stated the privilege belongs to the company, which decides whether to waive it and may disclose what is learned, including to the government. T4 then asked the witness to explain back who controls the privilege.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explained how the interview would run, asked for complete answers, told the witness to flag speculation, and asked them to say whether they remember or are reconstructing. It did not expressly say speculation is allowed.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asked the witness to restate who is represented and who controls privilege, and the witness did so correctly at T5. T6 then addressed the right to consult personal counsel and asked whether the witness was comfortable.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T64 asked whether anything was left out, and T68 gave a confidentiality reminder, a record-retention instruction, a no-discussion-with-witnesses instruction, and a note that the Committee may follow up. The close did not confirm next steps in detail.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
This interview is confidential and privileged, but that privilege belongs to the company, not to you or to us.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
You represent the company. The company controls the privilege. Can we move on?

Explained the interview structure, asked for complete answers, asked the witness to flag speculation and to say whether they remember or are reconstructing, and noted the right to consult their own lawyer.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Only the LJM1 question at T14 was a true open invitation. Most later topics, including Southampton and Chewco, were asked narrowly and in closed form.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moved sensibly from role (T8) to LJM1 (T14), then the Board, Rhythms, Southampton and Chewco, and finally controls, narrowing each topic in turn.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were clear and short. T42 was compound ('Did you tell the Board, Mr. Lay, or Mr. Skilling about the Foundation's investment?'), and T56 assumed its premise.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stayed polite and neutral despite the witness's curt 'Let's get on with it' at T1 and terse answers, and kept control of the questioning, for example at T40.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer adjusted when the witness deflected: T38 used a specific figure after the vague 'several million' at T37, and T40 and T44 pressed on the Foundation point. It did not follow up on the 'It's in the minutes' deflection at T25.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Started with the witness's role and moved through LJM1, the Board, Rhythms, Southampton and Chewco in a logical sequence.
Did you tell the Board, Mr. Lay, or Mr. Skilling about the Foundation's investment?
How do you know Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy reviewed every LJM2 deal?
The witness opened with 'Let's get on with it', and the interviewer replied politely and stayed in control of the questioning.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: T24 probed how sure the witness was, and T58 and T62 followed up on approval sheets and asked which ones. The interviewer did not press 'It's in the minutes' at T25 or 'Not personally' at T59.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked who first suggested the GP role (T18 and T20), what was told to the Board (T22), who negotiated the unwind (T26 to T29), and who was told about the Foundation (T42 to T44). Timing questions were rare.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: After the witness said 'I'd have to check' at T37, the interviewer supplied the $4.5M figure at T38. No other technique was tried when the witness could not recall, such as asking about the minutes or the record.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: T42 to T45 separated what the witness personally did ('Not by me') from what others knew. The interviewer did not ask how the witness knew what the minutes said (T25) or separate speculation from knowledge on the Foundation.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T66 asked who else to speak with, and the witness named Causey, Buy and Kopper. Glisan, named earlier at T13, was not raised.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer showed the November 5, 1997 minutes. The witness said the approval sheets 'would show it' at T63, but the interviewer did not ask for those records, the Foundation records, or other communications.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: T58 asked whether the witness checked that approvals were followed, and T59 got the answer 'Not personally'. T24 tested certainty about the Board statement, and the witness deflected to the minutes.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers were followed up: T40 to T45 on the Foundation, T49 to T51 on disclosure, and T61 to T63 on approval sheets. The 'investment vehicle' answer at T31 and 'It happened' at T61 were not probed on what they meant.

moments.text: How sure are you that's what you told them?
It's in the minutes.
Our information is roughly $4.5 million, about six weeks after it invested. Does that fit your memory?
How does that fit with what you told the Board about not receiving value from the Enron stock?
Did you check that it was followed?
Not personally.
Which ones?
Raptor I, maybe others. The sheets would show it.
Who else should we speak with?
Causey. Buy. Kopper.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The interviewer authenticated the minutes at T52 by asking if the witness recognized them, and the witness said they looked like the Committee's minutes at T53. The document was not contextualised beyond that.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The witness's account of Kopper's Chewco role was taken at T46 to T51 before the minutes were shown at T52. The interviewer did not ask what the witness remembered about the November 5 meeting before showing the document.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The question at T54 ('Do they mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?') accurately reflects what the minutes do and do not record. The interviewer did not characterise the document further.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: T54 asked an open question about the document rather than stating a conclusion, although its framing leans toward a particular answer.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: After the witness said 'No' at T55, the interviewer moved on without asking the witness to reconcile that answer with the disclosure claim at T51.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
They look like the Committee's minutes.
Do they mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?
No.
If a senior officer were involved, it would have to be in the proxy.

T25: The witness answered 'It's in the minutes' about what was told to the Board. The interviewer did not ask which minutes, or what they say, to test the witness's certainty.
